items.title: GTA VI Breaks All-Time Sales Record
points: GTA VI earned $3.79 billion in first-day sales, nearly 5x GTA V's 2013 launch revenue.
Sales exceeded the highest-grossing film ever.

items.title: SEC Opens Probe into Nvidia's Accounting
points: SEC launched a civil investigation (non-criminal inquiry by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission) into whether Nvidia misled investors; no criminal allegations have been made yet.
Focus centers on $104 billion in Singapore sales (47% of Nvidia's revenue) and customer Megaspeed, suspected of rerouting Nvidia chips to restricted buyers in China.
Nvidia stock fell 14% on Friday, erasing $485 billion in market value and roughly $2.7 trillion since its October 6 peak.

items.title: YouTube Nears $3B Settlement Over School Addiction Claims
points: YouTube nears a $3 billion settlement with school districts in lawsuits claiming its addictive design harmed students' mental health.
This would be the largest-ever corporate settlement with U.S. schools over social media's impact on teens.
The payout (~$1 million per district if split evenly among thousands of districts) is under 1% of Alphabet's $280 billion+ annual revenue; YouTube also promised unspecified new safeguards.

items.title: Meta Abandons 2030 Net-Zero Emissions Target
points: Meta scrapped its goal of net-zero emissions (balancing out all greenhouse gases it emits) by 2030 as pollution surged 45% year-over-year to 21.7 million metric tonnes, up from 15.6 million in 2024.
The increase matches Idaho's annual carbon footprint and is the largest emissions surge among major tech companies.
Meta attributed the change to AI data center expansion growing faster than anticipated, forcing a re-evaluation of climate timelines.

items.title: Trump Threatens Tax on Offshore Data Centers
points: Trump threatened a 'tremendous tax' on U.S. companies building data centers abroad.

Major tech firms already operate international facilities to serve local customers and comply with data residency rules (laws requiring data about a country's citizens to be stored within that country).

items.title: FBI Investigates Crime Database Breach
points: The National Crime Information Center (NCIC), used nationwide by police to check warrants and run background checks, appears to have been breached.
A former FBI official told CNN the accuracy of crime records nationwide is now in question, beyond privacy concerns.
The breach was discovered Thursday, the same day FBI Director Kash Patel promoted 'Operation Winter Shield' on Fox News despite it having ended months earlier.
